subject: WL
overview: Spanish II meets about 50 minutes a day and follows a weekly rhythm: new grammar or vocabulary early in the week, authentic reading/listening and conversation midweek, and a quiz, project, or performance assessment on Friday. Speak Spanish as much as possible, model each structure aloud before practice, and expect the student to speak and write every day. You do not need to be fluent: use the answers given here, SpanishDict for conjugations, and recordings of native speakers, and reteach any structure scored below 80% before moving on.

weeks.prep: Set up the Spanish notebook with sections (vocabulario, gramática, escritura) and create the Conjuguemos account. Make a present-tense chart for -ar/-er/-ir endings plus ser, estar, tener, ir, and the yo-go verbs. Have a phone ready to record the self-introduction.
misconceptions: Using 'estar' for personality (Estoy simpático): personality and traits use ser (Soy simpático); estar is for location and temporary states (Estoy cansado).
Saying 'Yo gusto la pizza': gustar works backward — the thing liked is the subject: Me gusta la pizza; Me gustan los perros.
Applying yo-go to every form (*nosotros tengamos): only the yo form adds -go (tengo); tener is also e→ie in other forms (tienes, tiene, tenemos).

days.guide: Model a short introduction aloud: 'Me llamo Ana. Tengo quince años. Soy creativa y un poco tímida. Me gusta leer y me gustan los gatos.' Your child writes a script with ser, tener, and gustar, practices it twice, then records about one minute; check for 'tengo ... años' (not 'soy ... años').

questions.q: How do you say 'I am 15 years old' in Spanish?
questions.a: Tengo quince años. (Age uses tener, not ser.)

questions.q: Say 'I like dogs' and 'I like to read.'
questions.a: Me gustan los perros. Me gusta leer. (gustan with a plural noun; gusta with an infinitive.)

days.guide: Review the endings: -ar (o, as, a, amos, áis, an), -er (o, es, e, emos, éis, en), -ir (o, es, e, imos, ís, en). Your child completes the Conjuguemos set, then writes 10 sentences about the week; check that each verb matches its subject.

questions.q: Conjugate vivir for nosotros and comer for ellos.
questions.a: vivimos; comen

questions.q: Translate: 'We study Spanish on Mondays.'
questions.a: Estudiamos español los lunes.

days.guide: Chant the yo-go forms (tengo, hago, salgo, pongo, vengo, digo, traigo) and show stem-changers as 'boot verbs' (all forms change except nosotros/vosotros). Your child does the timed drill twice and tries to beat the first time.

questions.q: Give the yo form of hacer, salir, and poner.
questions.a: hago, salgo, pongo

questions.q: Conjugate poder for tú and nosotros.
questions.a: puedes; podemos (nosotros does not change: o→ue only inside the 'boot').

days.guide: Help your child write 10 questions with question words (¿Cómo te llamas? ¿Qué te gusta hacer? ¿Dónde vives? ¿Cuántos hermanos tienes?). They interview you or a pen pal in Spanish and write the answers in third person (Mi mamá se llama...).

questions.q: Write the question 'Where do you live?' and answer it.
questions.a: ¿Dónde vives? — Vivo en (ciudad).

questions.q: Change 'Me gusta cocinar' to report what your mother said.
questions.a: A mi mamá le gusta cocinar.

days.guide: Give the present-tense quiz with notes closed. Grade it together, have your child correct each error with the rule, and score the recording with the rubric.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'Yo soy cansado hoy.'
questions.a: Yo estoy cansado hoy — a temporary condition uses estar.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz (aim 80%+): sample key — hablar/yo: hablo; comer/tú: comes; vivir/nosotros: vivimos; tener/ella: tiene; hacer/yo: hago; salir/yo: salgo; poner/yo: pongo; querer/ellos: quieren; poder/tú: puedes; pedir/nosotros: pedimos. Recording rubric (4 pts each): 4 = 1 full minute, name/age/personality/likes all included, correct ser/tener/gustar, clear pronunciation; 3 = all content, 1–2 errors; 2 = missing a part or frequent errors; 1 = very short or mostly English.

weeks.prep: Make or print picture cards for the daily routine (waking, showering, brushing teeth, dressing, going to bed) and set out a clock with movable hands. Find a short Spanish 'mi rutina' video (search 'mi rutina diaria' on YouTube) and preview it.
misconceptions: Dropping the reflexive pronoun (Despierto a las seis): with reflexive verbs the pronoun matches the subject — Me despierto a las seis.
Attaching the pronoun wrongly (Me voy a ducharme): either 'Me voy a duchar' or 'Voy a ducharme', not both.
Forgetting stem changes inside reflexives: despertarse (e→ie) me despierto; acostarse (o→ue) me acuesto; vestirse (e→i) me visto.

days.guide: Show the pronoun chart (me, te, se, nos, os, se) and act out 'me lavo las manos' vs. 'lavo el carro' to show the action returns to the subject. Your child conjugates 10 routine verbs and labels the picture cards; check the pronouns and stem changes.

questions.q: Conjugate levantarse for yo, tú, and ellos.
questions.a: me levanto, te levantas, se levantan

questions.q: Why is it 'Me lavo las manos' and not 'Me lavo mis manos'?
questions.a: With reflexive verbs, Spanish uses the definite article for body parts because the pronoun already shows whose hands they are.

days.guide: Model telling time with a routine: 'A las seis y media me despierto. A las siete menos cuarto me ducho.' Your child writes the full weekday routine with times; check 'a la una' (singular) vs. 'a las dos'.

questions.q: Write 'At 7:15 I get dressed.'
questions.a: A las siete y cuarto me visto.

questions.q: Write 'At 1:00 I eat lunch.'
questions.a: A la una almuerzo.

days.guide: Play the routine video once just to listen, then again pausing to fill a timeline (time + activity). Your child compares the timeline with the speaker's words and you check two items by replaying.

questions.q: If the speaker says 'Me acuesto a las once de la noche,' what time does he go to bed?

days.guide: Explain that in Spain dinner is often around 9–10 p.m., the main meal (la comida) is around 2–3 p.m., and the long midday break is more common than a daily nap. Your child fills a Venn diagram comparing their routine to a Spanish teen's and writes 3 comparison sentences.

questions.q: Write a comparison: 'I eat dinner at 6; a teen in Spain eats at 9.'
questions.a: Yo ceno a las seis, pero un joven en España cena a las nueve.

questions.q: What is 'la comida' in Spain?
questions.a: The main midday meal, usually eaten around 2–3 p.m.

days.guide: Give the reflexive quiz, then have your child describe the routine aloud from memory using times and transition words (primero, luego, después, finalmente). Score with the rubric.

questions.q: Say 'First I wake up, then I shower, and finally I get dressed.'
questions.a: Primero me despierto, luego me ducho y finalmente me visto.

weeks.assessment_key: Reflexive quiz sample key: 1) yo/levantarse — me levanto 2) tú/ducharse — te duchas 3) ella/vestirse — se viste 4) nosotros/acostarse — nos acostamos 5) ellos/despertarse — se despiertan 6) yo/cepillarse los dientes — me cepillo los dientes. Oral routine rubric: 4 = 8+ routine actions in order with times and correct pronouns; 3 = 6–7 actions, minor errors; 2 = under 6 actions or frequent pronoun errors; 1 = isolated words.

weeks.prep: Copy the child's class schedule onto the template; prepare stem-changer playing cards (verb on one side, subject on the other). Find a short reading on a school day in Mexico or Argentina (e.g., a textbook reading or a Spanish blog about 'la escuela secundaria').
misconceptions: Changing the stem in nosotros (*empiezamos): nosotros and vosotros keep the original stem — empezamos, almorzamos, pedimos.
Confusing e→ie and e→i: preferir becomes prefiero (ie), but pedir becomes pido (i). Memorize each with its pattern.
Saying 'Me gusta la matemática' for school subjects: the subject is usually plural — Me gustan las matemáticas.

days.guide: Model: 'Tengo matemáticas a las nueve. Me gustan porque son interesantes, pero son difíciles.' Your child writes 10 sentences about classes and opinions; check that adjectives agree with the subject (las ciencias son fascinantes).

questions.q: Write 'History is boring but art is fun.'
questions.a: La historia es aburrida, pero el arte es divertido.

questions.q: How do you say 'school subject' and 'schedule'?
questions.a: la asignatura (or la materia); el horario

days.guide: Sort verbs into three 'boots': e→ie (empezar, querer, preferir), o→ue (almorzar, poder, dormir), e→i (pedir, servir, repetir). Play the card game: flip a verb and a subject and say the form; then complete the written drill.

questions.q: Conjugate almorzar for yo and nosotros.
questions.a: almuerzo; almorzamos

questions.q: Conjugate pedir for ella.
questions.a: pide

days.guide: Read the article together; your child lists five differences (e.g., uniforms, morning or afternoon shifts called turnos in Mexico, students staying in one classroom while teachers move, calling teachers 'maestro/profe'). Check that each difference comes from the reading.

questions.q: Write a sentence about a difference: 'In Mexico, many students wear uniforms.'
questions.a: En México, muchos estudiantes llevan uniforme.

days.guide: Act out a conversation: '¿Qué prefieres hacer después de las clases?' — 'Prefiero jugar al fútbol. ¿Y tú?' Your child must use preferir and querer at least three times each and ask follow-up questions.

questions.q: Answer: '¿Qué quieres hacer esta tarde?' (You want to swim.)
questions.a: Quiero nadar esta tarde.

questions.q: Ask a friend 'Do you prefer soccer or basketball?'
questions.a: ¿Prefieres el fútbol o el básquetbol?

days.guide: Give the stem-changer quiz and score the role-play from day 4 with the rubric. Have your child re-conjugate any missed verb in all six forms.

questions.q: Conjugate dormir in all six present forms.
questions.a: duermo, duermes, duerme, dormimos, dormís, duermen

weeks.assessment_key: Stem-changer quiz sample key: empezar/yo — empiezo; almorzar/tú — almuerzas; preferir/ella — prefiere; pedir/nosotros — pedimos; querer/ellos — quieren; dormir/yo — duermo; servir/tú — sirves; poder/ustedes — pueden; volver/él — vuelve; repetir/yo — repito. Role-play rubric: 4 = asks and answers 5+ questions with correct stem changes and natural follow-ups; 3 = 4 exchanges, few errors; 2 = short answers, several errors; 1 = cannot sustain.

weeks.prep: Print the IPA task sheet and find an authentic school-schedule or school-life article (e.g., from a Spanish-language school website or a teen magazine). Plan the 3-minute conversation prompts and gather Unit 1 flashcards. Write the unit test covering present tense, reflexives, stem-changers, routine, and school vocabulary.
misconceptions: Translating word-for-word from English in the email: encourage short, known structures (Me levanto a las siete) rather than invented phrases.
Forgetting greetings and closings in an email: use 'Hola, ...' / 'Querido/a ...' and 'Un abrazo' or 'Saludos'.

days.guide: Your child reads the article independently, highlighting cognates first, then answers the comprehension questions in English or simple Spanish. Afterward, discuss which clues (cognates, numbers, times) helped.

questions.q: What strategy helps when you meet an unknown word in an authentic text?
questions.a: Look for cognates (e.g., 'horario' near times and class names), use context, and skip words not needed for the question.

days.guide: Hold the 3-minute conversation using questions like ¿A qué hora te levantas? ¿Cuál es tu clase favorita? ¿Qué haces después de las clases? Keep it natural; note errors but don't interrupt. Score with the rubric.

questions.q: How would you answer '¿A qué hora te acuestas?' (11:00 p.m.)
questions.a: Me acuesto a las once de la noche.

days.guide: Your child writes the 150-word email to a new exchange student, including a greeting, routine with times, classes, and a question for the student. Check reflexive pronouns and word count.

questions.q: Write a good closing sentence asking a question back.
questions.a: Example: ¿Y tú? ¿Cómo es tu rutina? ¡Escríbeme pronto! Saludos, (nombre)

days.guide: Review all Unit 1 flashcards; sort into 'know' and 'don't know' piles and redo the second pile until it is empty. Your child corrects errors from the IPA tasks and writes the rule beside each.

questions.q: Translate: 'to brush one's teeth,' 'to get up,' 'to go to bed.'
questions.a: cepillarse los dientes, levantarse, acostarse

days.guide: Give the Unit 1 test without notes. Grade, go over errors together, and log scores.

questions.q: Correct: 'Nosotros nos acuestamos tarde.'
questions.a: Nosotros nos acostamos tarde (no stem change in nosotros).

weeks.assessment_key: IPA rubric (each mode, 4 levels): Interpretive — 4 = identifies main idea and 5+ details accurately; 3 = main idea and 3–4 details; 2 = some details; 1 = isolated words. Interpersonal — 4 = sustains 3 minutes, asks and answers questions, mostly accurate present/reflexive verbs; 3 = sustains with some pauses; 2 = mostly short answers; 1 = cannot sustain. Presentational — 4 = ~150 words, greeting/closing, routine in sequence with times, accurate reflexives; 3 = complete with minor errors; 2 = under 100 words or many errors; 1 = fragments. Unit test sample items: me ducho; nosotros almorzamos; ella se viste; 'A las ocho y media empiezo las clases.'

weeks.prep: Gather 3–5 childhood photos. Make an imperfect chart: -ar: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban; -er/-ir: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían; irregulars ser (era), ir (iba), ver (veía).
misconceptions: Forgetting the accent on -ía (*comia): every -er/-ir imperfect form has an accent on the í (comía, vivíamos).
Missing the accent on nosotros -ar (*hablabamos): it is hablábamos.
Using the preterite for habitual past actions: 'used to / would' habits take the imperfect (Siempre jugaba en el parque).

days.guide: Explain that the imperfect describes how things were or used to be. Model 'De niña, yo jugaba mucho y comía helado.' Your child conjugates the 20 verbs; check accents.

questions.q: Conjugate estudiar in the imperfect for yo and nosotros.
questions.a: estudiaba; estudiábamos

questions.q: Conjugate escribir for ellos.
questions.a: escribían

days.guide: List frequency words (siempre, a menudo, todos los días, cada verano, a veces, nunca). Your child writes 10 'used to' sentences about childhood, each with a frequency word.

questions.q: Translate: 'Every summer we used to go to the beach.'
questions.a: Cada verano íbamos a la playa.

questions.q: Translate: 'I often watched cartoons.'
questions.a: A menudo veía dibujos animados.

days.guide: Teach the only three irregulars: ser (era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran), ir (iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban), ver (veía, veías...). Your child writes two sentences for each.

questions.q: Translate: 'My grandmother was very kind.'
questions.a: Mi abuela era muy amable.

questions.q: Translate: 'We used to go to the park.'
questions.a: Íbamos al parque.

days.guide: Your child chooses a photo and describes it aloud: age (Tenía cinco años), place (Vivíamos en...), people, and what they used to do. Ask two follow-up questions.

questions.q: How do you say 'I was five years old'?
questions.a: Tenía cinco años (age in the past uses tener in the imperfect).

days.guide: Give the imperfect quiz and score the photo description with the rubric. Review any missed accents.

questions.q: Fill in: Cuando yo ___ (ser) niño, ___ (vivir) en Texas.
questions.a: era; vivía

weeks.assessment_key: Imperfect quiz sample key: hablar/yo — hablaba; comer/nosotros — comíamos; vivir/ellos — vivían; jugar/tú — jugabas; ser/yo — era; ir/nosotros — íbamos; ver/ella — veía; tener/ustedes — tenían; 'When I was little, I used to play soccer' — Cuando era pequeño/a, jugaba al fútbol. Photo description rubric: 4 = 6+ imperfect sentences describing age, place, people, and activities, accurate forms; 3 = 4–5 sentences; 2 = few verbs or mixed tenses; 1 = isolated words.

weeks.prep: Find short Spanish readings or videos on rayuela (hopscotch), trompo (spinning top), lotería, and canicas (marbles). Print or buy a lotería set (printable sets are free online) and prepare a Venn diagram.
misconceptions: Thinking lotería is a number game like bingo: it uses pictures with names (El gallo, La sirena, La luna), often called with a riddle or rhyme.
Assuming games are identical across cultures: many are shared (hide-and-seek = escondidas/escondite) but names and rules vary by country.

days.guide: Read the short texts together, pausing to match each game with a picture. Your child writes one sentence per game in Spanish (La rayuela es un juego con tiza y una piedra).

questions.q: What is la rayuela?
questions.a: Hopscotch — a chalk grid where you toss a stone and hop through the squares.

questions.q: What do you need to play el trompo?
questions.a: A wooden top and a string (cuerda) to wind and throw it.

days.guide: Play lotería: the caller (your child first) reads each card in Spanish; players mark with beans. Switch callers so everyone practices pronunciation.

questions.q: What do players say when they win?
questions.a: ¡Lotería! (some families also say ¡Buenas!)

days.guide: Your child asks a family member: ¿A qué jugabas de niño? ¿Con quién jugabas? ¿Dónde jugaban? and takes notes in Spanish using the imperfect.

questions.q: Write the question 'What did you used to play when you were a child?'
questions.a: ¿A qué jugabas cuando eras niño/a?

questions.q: Report: 'My dad used to play marbles with his brothers.'
questions.a: Mi papá jugaba a las canicas con sus hermanos.

days.guide: Your child compares two games (e.g., U.S. hopscotch vs. rayuela, or bingo vs. lotería) in a Venn diagram and writes three comparison sentences in Spanish.

questions.q: Write: 'Both games use cards.'
questions.a: Los dos juegos usan cartas (or tarjetas).

days.guide: Give the short reading check and review the interview notes with the rubric.

questions.q: How do you say 'to hide' and 'hide-and-seek'?
questions.a: esconderse; las escondidas (Latin America) or el escondite (Spain)

weeks.assessment_key: Reading check sample key: 1) La rayuela = hopscotch, drawn with chalk and played by tossing a stone; 2) El trompo = a wooden spinning top wound with string; 3) La lotería = a Mexican picture game played with tablas and frijoles as markers; 4) Las canicas = marbles; 5) 'jugar a las escondidas' = to play hide-and-seek. Interview notes rubric: 4 = 8+ notes in Spanish using the imperfect (Mi papá jugaba...), with details on where/with whom; 3 = 5–7 notes; 2 = few notes or mostly English; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Gather drawing paper. Find a short story told in the imperfect (a Spanish-learner podcast like 'Cuentos de mi niñez' or a graded reader). Prepare a list of describing adjectives (alto, bajo, simpático, travieso, tranquilo).
misconceptions: Using 'era' for location (*La casa era en el centro): location uses estar — La casa estaba en el centro.
Pluralizing 'había' (*habían muchos árboles): había (there was/were) is always singular — Había muchos árboles.
Adjective agreement errors: mi maestra era simpática (feminine), mis vecinos eran ruidosos (plural).

days.guide: Model: 'Mi casa era grande. Tenía tres dormitorios. Había un parque cerca.' Your child draws the childhood home and neighborhood and writes 8 sentences using era, tenía, había, and estaba.

questions.q: Translate: 'There were many children in my neighborhood.'
questions.a: Había muchos niños en mi vecindario (barrio).

questions.q: Translate: 'The school was near my house.'
questions.a: La escuela estaba cerca de mi casa.

days.guide: Your child writes a 6-sentence description of a friend or teacher: appearance (era alto, tenía pelo rizado), personality, and what they used to do together.

questions.q: Translate: 'She had brown eyes and was very funny.'
questions.a: Tenía ojos marrones (or café) y era muy graciosa (or divertida).

days.guide: Play the story twice; your child answers questions and lists imperfect verbs heard. Discuss how the imperfect sets the scene.

questions.q: Why does a story often begin 'Había una vez...'?
questions.a: It means 'Once upon a time there was...' — the imperfect sets background, like describing the scene.

days.guide: Use prompts: ¿Dónde vivías? ¿Cómo era tu escuela? ¿Quién era tu mejor amigo? You answer about your own childhood; your child compares (Yo vivía en..., pero tú vivías en...).

questions.q: Ask: 'What was your school like?'
questions.a: ¿Cómo era tu escuela?

days.guide: Give the writing quiz: describe a childhood place and a person in at least 8 sentences. Score with the rubric.

questions.q: Correct: 'Habían muchos árboles y la casa era en una calle tranquila.'
questions.a: Había muchos árboles y la casa estaba en una calle tranquila.

weeks.assessment_key: Writing quiz rubric (descriptive paragraph in the past): 4 = 8+ sentences, correct era/estaba/tenía/había, adjectives agree, varied vocabulary; 3 = 6–7 sentences, few errors; 2 = 4–5 sentences or frequent errors; 1 = fragments. Proficient sample: 'Mi casa era pequeña y azul. Estaba cerca de un parque. Había un árbol grande en el jardín. Mi vecina se llamaba Rosa; era alta y muy simpática.'

weeks.prep: Gather photos or drawings, construction paper or a slide template, and glue. Print an editing checklist: imperfect endings and accents, ser/ir/ver forms, noun–adjective agreement. Write the Unit 2 test (imperfect forms, childhood vocabulary, games, describing the past).
misconceptions: Mixing present tense into captions (Vivo en...): captions about childhood need the imperfect (Vivía en...).
Reading the presentation word-for-word: use photos as cues and speak from memory.

days.guide: Help your child choose a photo or drawing for each page topic: home, family, school, games, food, holidays. List key vocabulary for each page in the notebook.

questions.q: Give a Spanish title for the food page.
questions.a: Example: La comida de mi niñez / Lo que comía de niño/a

days.guide: Your child writes 3–4 imperfect captions per page (Vivíamos en una casa amarilla. Siempre jugaba con mi perro.). Circulate and point out good examples.

questions.q: Write a caption: 'On holidays we always ate tamales.'
questions.a: En los días festivos siempre comíamos tamales.

days.guide: Your child edits with the checklist, underlining every verb and checking its ending and accent. You spot-check one page and mark errors with a symbol (not the correction).

questions.q: Find and fix: 'Mis abuelos vivia en Chicago.'
questions.a: Mis abuelos vivían en Chicago.

days.guide: Your child presents the book for 2 minutes using pictures as cues, then answers two questions you ask (¿Cuál era tu juguete favorito? ¿Qué te gustaba comer?).

questions.q: Answer: '¿Cuál era tu juguete favorito?'
questions.a: Example: Mi juguete favorito era un oso de peluche.

days.guide: Give the Unit 2 test. Grade and review.

questions.q: Conjugate ver in the imperfect for all forms.
questions.a: veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían

weeks.assessment_key: Memory book rubric: Content — 6 pages with 3–4 captions each; Language — accurate imperfect forms and agreement; Presentation — 2 minutes, not read, answers 2 questions; Visuals — clear and labeled. 4 = all criteria met with few errors; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = missing pages or many errors; 1 = incomplete. Unit test sample: 1) nosotros/ir — íbamos 2) yo/ver — veía 3) ellos/ser — eran 4) 'jugábamos a las canicas' = we used to play marbles 5) 'Había' = there was/were.

weeks.prep: Make a preterite chart: -ar: -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron; -er/-ir: -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. Have a calendar to talk about 'ayer, anoche, la semana pasada'.
misconceptions: Missing accents that change meaning: hablo (I speak) vs. habló (he spoke).
Forgetting spelling changes in yo forms: buscar → busqué, llegar → llegué, empezar → empecé.
Confusing nosotros forms: -ar/-ir nosotros are the same in present and preterite (hablamos, vivimos); context and time words tell which.

days.guide: Explain the preterite tells completed actions at a specific time. Model 'Ayer comí pizza y miré una película.' Your child conjugates 20 verbs; check accents on yo and él forms.

questions.q: Conjugate cantar in the preterite for yo, él, and ellos.
questions.a: canté, cantó, cantaron

questions.q: Conjugate salir for tú.
questions.a: saliste

days.guide: Review time expressions (ayer, anoche, anteayer, el fin de semana pasado, el año pasado). Your child writes 10 sentences about yesterday or last weekend.

questions.q: Translate: 'Last night I studied and then I slept.'
questions.a: Anoche estudié y luego dormí.

days.guide: Show why: to keep the sound, c→qu, g→gu, z→c before é. Practice busqué, saqué, toqué, llegué, pagué, jugué, empecé, almorcé, comencé.

questions.q: Give the yo preterite of tocar, pagar, and almorzar.
questions.a: toqué, pagué, almorcé

questions.q: Why is 'él buscó' spelled with c but 'yo busqué' with qu?
questions.a: Before o the c already sounds like k; before é it must be qu to keep the k sound.

days.guide: Your child writes a 120-word paragraph about the last birthday: who came, what you ate, what you did. Check that all completed actions are in the preterite.

questions.q: Translate: 'My cousins came and we ate cake.'
questions.a: Mis primos vinieron y comimos pastel (or torta).

questions.q: Translate: 'I opened the gifts.'
questions.a: Abrí los regalos.

days.guide: Give the preterite quiz and review any spelling-change errors.

questions.q: Fill in: Ayer yo ___ (llegar) tarde y ___ (empezar) la tarea a las nueve.
questions.a: llegué; empecé

weeks.assessment_key: Preterite quiz sample key: hablar/yo — hablé; comer/tú — comiste; vivir/ella — vivió; bailar/nosotros — bailamos; abrir/ellos — abrieron; buscar/yo — busqué; llegar/yo — llegué; empezar/yo — empecé; jugar/yo — jugué; celebrar/ustedes — celebraron.

weeks.prep: Gather ofrenda materials (photo, candles or LED candles, paper marigolds or cempasúchil images, papel picado, small foods) or a slide template. Preview a respectful reading on Día de los Muertos. Chart the irregular preterites: ser/ir (fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron), hacer (hice, hiciste, hizo...), tener (tuve...), estar (estuve...), poder (pude...).
misconceptions: Thinking Día de los Muertos is 'Mexican Halloween': it is a celebration (Nov. 1–2) honoring and remembering loved ones who have died, not a scary holiday.
Adding accents to irregular preterites (*tuvó, *hizó): the irregular 'stem' preterites have no written accents — tuve, tuvo, hice, hizo.
Confusing fui = 'I went' and 'I was': ser and ir share preterite forms; context decides.

days.guide: Teach the irregulars as patterns (hacer: hic/hiz-, tener: tuv-, estar: estuv-, poder: pud-, all with endings -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron). Drill with quick oral prompts.

questions.q: Translate: 'We went to the cemetery.'
questions.a: Fuimos al cementerio.

questions.q: Conjugate hacer for él.
questions.a: hizo (z keeps the soft sound before o)

days.guide: Read about traditions: ofrendas, cempasúchil (marigolds whose color and scent guide spirits), pan de muerto, calaveras, visits to graves. Your child lists five traditions and their meanings.

questions.q: Why are marigolds (cempasúchil) used?
questions.a: Their bright color and scent are believed to guide the spirits of loved ones back to the ofrenda.

questions.q: When is Día de los Muertos celebrated?
questions.a: November 1 and 2 (Nov. 1 often honors children, Nov. 2 adults).

days.guide: Your child builds a small or digital ofrenda for a relative or a historical figure (e.g., Frida Kahlo) and labels each item in Spanish with its meaning.

questions.q: What does the water on an ofrenda represent?
questions.a: It quenches the thirst of the spirits after their long journey.

days.guide: Your child writes a paragraph about a holiday they celebrated (Thanksgiving, a birthday, New Year) using at least 6 irregular preterites (fui, hice, tuve, estuve, pude).

questions.q: Translate: 'I was at my grandmother's house and we made tamales.'
questions.a: Estuve en la casa de mi abuela e hicimos tamales.

days.guide: Give the irregular preterite quiz and check the ofrenda labels with the rubric.

questions.q: Fill in: Ellos no ___ (poder) venir porque ___ (tener) que trabajar.
questions.a: pudieron; tuvieron

weeks.assessment_key: Irregular quiz sample key: ir/yo — fui; ser/ella — fue; hacer/él — hizo; hacer/nosotros — hicimos; tener/tú — tuviste; estar/ellos — estuvieron; poder/yo — pude; tener/nosotros — tuvimos. Ofrenda label rubric: 4 = 8+ items labeled correctly in Spanish (la vela, el cempasúchil, el pan de muerto, el papel picado, la foto, el agua, la calavera de azúcar) with a sentence explaining the meaning of each; 3 = 6–7; 2 = 4–5; 1 = fewer.

weeks.prep: Print a few short comic strips (or draw 6 simple panels). Make a two-column chart: Imperfecto (background, description, habit, ongoing action, time/age, emotions) vs. Pretérito (completed action, specific time, sequence, interruption). Find a short story in the past (e.g., a graded reader chapter).
misconceptions: Thinking a 'long' action must be imperfect: duration does not decide; 'Viví en Texas diez años' is preterite because the period is completed and bounded.
Using the preterite for the scene-setting (*Fue un día bonito y hizo sol) at the start of a story: background description normally uses the imperfect (Era un día bonito y hacía sol).
Not recognizing the interruption pattern: the ongoing action is imperfect and the interrupting one preterite — Leía cuando sonó el teléfono.

days.guide: Use the chart and a 'movie' analogy: the imperfect is the scenery and ongoing action; the preterite is the events that move the plot. Model a 4-sentence story labeling each verb.

questions.q: Which tense: 'It was raining when I left' (llover / salir)?
questions.a: Llovía (background, imperfect) cuando salí (completed event, preterite).

questions.q: Which tense for telling age in the past: 'She was 10'?
questions.a: Imperfect: Tenía diez años.

days.guide: Your child completes 25 sentences, writing the reason code beside each (H = habit, D = description, C = completed, I = interruption). Check the reasons, not just answers.

questions.q: Choose: Mientras yo (estudiaba/estudié), mi hermano (miraba/miró) la tele.
questions.a: estudiaba; miraba — two simultaneous ongoing actions with mientras.

days.guide: Read a short story; your child highlights imperfect verbs in one color and preterite in another and explains three of each.

questions.q: In 'Había una vez una niña que vivía en el bosque. Un día, salió de su casa', why does 'salió' change tense?
questions.a: Había/vivía set the scene; 'un día' signals a specific completed event, so salió is preterite.

days.guide: Your child narrates a 6-panel comic, writing at least two sentences per panel using both tenses and connectors (de repente, mientras, entonces, por fin).

questions.q: Write: 'Suddenly the dog ran into the street.'
questions.a: De repente el perro corrió a la calle.

days.guide: Give the tense quiz and score the comic with the rubric.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'Cuando era pequeño, fui a la playa todos los veranos.'
questions.a: Cuando era pequeño, iba a la playa todos los veranos (repeated habit = imperfect).

weeks.assessment_key: Tense quiz sample key: 1) Cuando era niño, siempre ___ (jugar) — jugaba (habit) 2) Ayer ___ (comer) a las dos — comí (completed) 3) ___ (Ser) las ocho cuando llegó — Eran (time) 4) Yo ___ (dormir) cuando sonó el teléfono — dormía (ongoing/interrupted) 5) De repente ___ (empezar) a llover — empezó (sudden action) 6) Mi abuela ___ (tener) pelo blanco — tenía (description). Comic narration rubric: 4 = 6 panels, both tenses used correctly for background vs. events, connectors (de repente, mientras, entonces); 3 = 1–2 tense errors; 2 = several; 1 = one tense only.

weeks.prep: Find a learner-level version of La Llorona (note: it is a ghost legend about a weeping woman who lost her children — preview for younger siblings). Prepare IPA questions and write the Unit 3 test (preterite regular/irregular, preterite vs. imperfect, celebrations vocabulary).
misconceptions: Using only the preterite in narratives: a strong story mixes background (imperfect) with events (preterite).
Forgetting irregular preterites under pressure (*tení, *hací): review tuve, hice, fui, estuve, pude.

days.guide: Your child reads the folktale independently and answers questions. Discuss why legends like this were told (to warn children away from rivers at night and to teach about consequences).

questions.q: What does 'llorona' mean and why is she called that?
questions.a: 'Weeping woman' — her ghost cries for her lost children.

questions.q: Which tense describes the setting of the legend ('vivía una mujer hermosa')?
questions.a: The imperfect.

days.guide: Take turns asking and answering about a memorable event: ¿Adónde fuiste? ¿Con quién fuiste? ¿Qué tiempo hacía? ¿Qué pasó? Your child must ask at least 6 questions.

questions.q: Ask 'What was the weather like?' in the past.
questions.a: ¿Qué tiempo hacía?

days.guide: Your child writes a 200-word narrative about a memorable trip or event, with a scene-setting opening in the imperfect and events in the preterite.

questions.q: Write an opening sentence setting the scene.
questions.a: Example: Era un sábado de julio y hacía mucho calor. Mi familia y yo estábamos en el carro.

days.guide: Your child makes a one-page study guide (charts of regular and irregular preterite, imperfect, and the tense-choice rules) and completes the Conjuguemos mixed-tense drill.

questions.q: List three irregular imperfect verbs.
questions.a: ser (era), ir (iba), ver (veía)

days.guide: Give the Unit 3 test and review errors.

questions.q: Fill in: Nosotros ___ (estar) en la fiesta cuando ___ (llegar) el payaso.
questions.a: estábamos; llegó

weeks.assessment_key: IPA rubric: Interpretive — 4 = sequences the main events of La Llorona (a woman loses her children in a river and her spirit wanders crying '¡Ay, mis hijos!') and answers detail questions accurately; Interpersonal — 4 = asks and answers 6+ questions about an event with correct past tenses; Presentational (200-word narrative) — 4 = clear beginning/middle/end, background in imperfect and events in preterite, 3+ connectors, few errors; 3 = minor errors; 2 = mostly one tense or under 150 words; 1 = fragments. Unit test sample: fui, hiciste, tuvimos, estuvieron; 'Hacía frío cuando llegamos' (imperfect + preterite).

weeks.prep: Gather sticky notes and a marker; collect a Spanish grocery ad (Vallarta, Northgate González, Cardenas, or a Spanish-language Walmart flyer). Chart indirect object pronouns (me, te, le, nos, os, les).
misconceptions: Making gustar agree with the person (*Yo gusto las fresas): agree with the thing liked — Me gustan las fresas.
Omitting the pronoun with 'a + person' (*A mi hermano gusta): it must be A mi hermano le gusta.
Using 'molestar' only as 'molest': in Spanish it simply means 'to bother/annoy' (Me molesta el ruido).

days.guide: Your child labels 40 foods with sticky notes, including articles (la manzana, el pan, las zanahorias). Quiz by pointing at items for a quick recall round.

questions.q: Give the Spanish for: rice, chicken, cheese, lettuce.
questions.a: el arroz, el pollo, el queso, la lechuga

days.guide: Show the pattern: (A mí) me + gusta(n) + thing. Teach encantar (love), interesar, molestar. Your child writes 10 sentences about family members using 'a + person' + pronoun.

questions.q: Translate: 'My brothers love pizza.'
questions.a: A mis hermanos les encanta la pizza.

questions.q: Translate: 'Spicy food bothers me.'
questions.a: Me molesta la comida picante.

days.guide: Read the grocery ad; your child creates a shopping list of 10 items with prices and a total under a budget (e.g., $40), writing quantities in Spanish (una libra de, una docena de).

questions.q: How do you say 'a dozen eggs' and 'a pound of beef'?
questions.a: una docena de huevos; una libra de carne de res

days.guide: Your child surveys family (¿Qué comida te encanta? ¿Qué comida te molesta?) and writes a report in third person.

questions.q: Report: 'My mom is interested in Mexican food.'
questions.a: A mi mamá le interesa la comida mexicana.

days.guide: Give the quiz and score the survey report.

questions.q: Correct: 'A mi abuela gusta los frijoles.'
questions.a: A mi abuela le gustan los frijoles.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz sample key: 1) (yo) encantar / las fresas — Me encantan las fresas 2) (ella) interesar / la cocina — Le interesa la cocina 3) (nosotros) molestar / la comida picante — Nos molesta la comida picante 4) (ellos) gustar / cocinar — Les gusta cocinar 5) la verdura = vegetable; la fruta = fruit; picante = spicy. Survey report rubric: 4 = 5+ people reported with correct pronouns (A mi papá le encanta..., A mis hermanos les molesta...) and a summary sentence; 3 = minor errors; 2 = many pronoun errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Find a real menu from a Mexican or Spanish restaurant (online). Chart direct object pronouns (me, te, lo, la, nos, os, los, las) and indirect (me, te, le, nos, os, les). Set up a table with a napkin and 'la cuenta' slip for the role-play.
misconceptions: Using 'le' for direct objects of things (*Le compré — the book): things take lo/la/los/las — Lo compré.
Putting the pronoun after a conjugated verb (*Compro lo): it goes before a conjugated verb (Lo compro) or attached to an infinitive (Voy a comprarlo).
Thinking tipping works the same everywhere: in Spain service is included in the price and small tips (rounding up) are customary but not required; in the U.S. 15–20% is expected.

days.guide: Model: '¿Tienes la tarea? — Sí, la tengo.' Your child replaces nouns with lo/la/los/las in 20 sentences, matching gender and number.

questions.q: Replace the noun: 'Compro las manzanas.'
questions.a: Las compro.

questions.q: Replace the noun: 'Voy a preparar el arroz.'
questions.a: Voy a prepararlo. / Lo voy a preparar.

days.guide: Indirect objects answer 'to/for whom.' Model 'El mesero me trae el agua. Le sirvo café a mi papá.' Your child writes sentences with traer and servir.

questions.q: Translate: 'The waiter brings us the menu.'
questions.a: El mesero nos trae el menú.

questions.q: Translate: 'I serve them soup.'
questions.a: Les sirvo sopa.

days.guide: You play the mesero: '¿Qué desean tomar?' Your child orders a full meal using usted, quiero/quisiera, and asks '¿Me trae la cuenta, por favor?'

questions.q: How do you politely ask for the check?
questions.a: La cuenta, por favor. / ¿Me trae la cuenta, por favor?

questions.q: How do you politely order: 'I would like the chicken'?
questions.a: Quisiera el pollo, por favor.

days.guide: Discuss la sobremesa (staying at the table to talk after a meal) and tipping differences. Your child writes 4 comparison sentences.

questions.q: What is 'la sobremesa'?
questions.a: The time spent relaxing and talking at the table after a meal; in Spain, servers don't rush you or bring the check until you ask.

days.guide: Give the pronoun quiz and score the role-play.

questions.q: Answer using a pronoun: '¿Pediste el postre?'
questions.a: Sí, lo pedí. / No, no lo pedí.

weeks.assessment_key: Pronoun quiz sample key: 1) Pido la sopa — La pido 2) Traigo los platos — Los traigo 3) Comemos las tortillas — Las comemos 4) El mesero trae el menú a nosotros — Nos trae el menú 5) Sirvo agua a mis padres — Les sirvo agua 6) Voy a pedir el flan — Voy a pedirlo / Lo voy a pedir. Role-play rubric: 4 = greets, orders drink/main/dessert, asks for la cuenta, uses usted and 2+ pronouns correctly; 3 = minor errors; 2 = incomplete; 1 = needs heavy prompting.

weeks.prep: Buy ingredients for guacamole (avocados, onion, tomato, cilantro, lime, salt, optional chile) or tortilla española (potatoes, eggs, onion, olive oil, salt). Find a Spanish recipe. Chart tú commands: affirmative regular = él form (corta, mezcla, añade); irregulars di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven; negative = no + subjunctive (no cortes, no pongas). Supervise knives and hot oil closely.
misconceptions: Forming negative tú commands from the affirmative (*No corta): negative uses the opposite vowel — No cortes, No comas.
Placing pronouns wrongly: attach to affirmative (Córtalo — add an accent) but put before negative (No lo cortes).
Forgetting the irregular yo stem in negatives: poner → no pongas, hacer → no hagas, salir → no salgas.

days.guide: Model with real actions: '¡Abre la puerta! ¡Pon la mesa! ¡Ven aquí!' Your child forms affirmative commands for 15 verbs and memorizes the 8 irregulars (Di Haz Ve Pon Sal Sé Ten Ven).

questions.q: Give affirmative tú commands for hacer, poner, and venir.
questions.a: haz, pon, ven

questions.q: Give the command for 'mix the eggs' using mezclar.
questions.a: Mezcla los huevos.

days.guide: Explain: start with yo, drop -o, add the opposite ending (-ar → -es, -er/-ir → -as). Your child rewrites 10 kitchen safety rules as negative commands.

questions.q: Write: 'Don't touch the hot pan.'
questions.a: No toques la sartén caliente.

questions.q: Write: 'Don't put the knife in the sink.'
questions.a: No pongas el cuchillo en el fregadero.

days.guide: Cook together using the Spanish recipe; your child reads each step aloud and you follow only what they say. Supervise knife and stove use.

questions.q: Translate 'Add salt and stir' as tú commands.
questions.a: Añade sal y revuelve (or mezcla).

days.guide: Your child records a 2-minute cooking show, giving at least 8 tú commands with sequence words.

questions.q: Rewrite with a pronoun: 'Corta los tomates.'
questions.a: Córtalos.

days.guide: Give the commands quiz and score the video.

questions.q: Make negative: 'Fríe las papas.'
questions.a: No frías las papas. (with pronoun: No las frías.)

weeks.assessment_key: Commands quiz sample key: 1) cortar — corta / no cortes 2) poner — pon / no pongas 3) hacer — haz / no hagas 4) venir — ven / no vengas 5) freír — fríe / no frías 6) añadir — añade / no añadas 7) mezclar los ingredientes with pronoun — Mézclalos 8) negative of Córtalo — No lo cortes. Cooking video rubric: 4 = 2 minutes, 8+ correct tú commands, clear sequence words (primero, luego, después), food vocabulary; 3 = 6–7 commands; 2 = under 6 or many errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Print a map of Latin America and Spain. Bookmark sources on paella (Valencia, Spain), arepas (Venezuela/Colombia), ceviche (Peru), mole (Puebla/Oaxaca, Mexico), pupusas (El Salvador), empanadas, asado (Argentina), gallo pinto (Costa Rica/Nicaragua), sancocho, and tortilla española.
misconceptions: Assuming all Spanish-speaking countries eat 'Mexican food': cuisines differ widely by region and ingredients (e.g., ceviche in Peru, asado in Argentina).
Misplacing dishes: paella is from Valencia, Spain; arepas are from Venezuela and Colombia; pupusas from El Salvador.

days.guide: Your child researches 4–6 dishes and records country, main ingredients, and one fact for each in Spanish.

questions.q: What is ceviche and where is it a national dish?
questions.a: Raw fish 'cooked' (marinated) in lime juice with onion and chile — Peru's national dish.

questions.q: Where is paella from and what grain is it made with?
questions.a: Valencia, Spain — rice (arroz), cooked in a wide pan.

days.guide: Your child marks 10 dishes on the map and writes one ingredient sentence for each (Las arepas se hacen con harina de maíz).

questions.q: Translate: 'Mole has chocolate and chiles.'
questions.a: El mole tiene chocolate y chiles.

questions.q: Where are pupusas from and what are they?
questions.a: El Salvador — thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, beans, or pork.

days.guide: Your child chooses one dish and outlines a 2-minute talk: origin, ingredients, history, when it is eaten, and a personal opinion. Practice once with notes.

questions.q: Write a sentence about when a dish is eaten: 'Tamales are eaten at Christmas.'
questions.a: Los tamales se comen en Navidad.

days.guide: Your child presents the dish (with a sample if possible). Ask two questions such as ¿Es picante? ¿Cuáles son los ingredientes principales?

questions.q: Answer: '¿Es difícil preparar la paella?'
questions.a: Example: Sí, es un poco difícil porque el arroz necesita mucho tiempo y atención.

days.guide: Your child reads a short article about a regional cuisine and answers 8 questions in Spanish. Check answers against the text.

questions.q: What does 'plato típico' mean?
questions.a: A traditional or signature dish of a region.

weeks.assessment_key: Dish presentation rubric: 4 = 2 minutes in Spanish, covers origin, main ingredients, history, and how/when it is eaten, accurate facts, answers 2 questions; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = under 1.5 minutes or inaccurate facts; 1 = incomplete. Reading comprehension key depends on the chosen article — the answers must quote or paraphrase the text in Spanish (e.g., for a ceviche article: El ceviche es de Perú; se prepara con pescado crudo marinado en jugo de limón).

weeks.prep: Assemble a review packet from Units 1–4: present, reflexive, preterite, imperfect, object pronouns, gustar-type verbs, and tú commands. Print a 15-item error-analysis sheet and the NCSSFL-ACTFL can-do statements (Novice High). Prepare a timed practice exam.
misconceptions: Double pronouns with affirmative commands: when attaching, add an accent to keep the stress (Prepáralo, Dámelo).
Shifting tenses randomly in narratives: decide for each verb whether it is background (imperfect) or an event (preterite).

days.guide: Your child completes the mixed drill, then rewrites a present-tense paragraph into the past, deciding preterite or imperfect for each verb.

questions.q: Rewrite in the past: 'Es sábado. Hace sol. Voy al mercado y compro frutas.'
questions.a: Era sábado. Hacía sol. Fui al mercado y compré frutas.

days.guide: Your child rewrites a recipe with commands and pronouns (Corta la cebolla → Córtala; No frías el huevo → No lo frías) and corrects the 15-item error sheet.

questions.q: Fix: 'No lo cortas.' (negative tú command)
questions.a: No lo cortes.

questions.q: Make affirmative with a pronoun: 'Pon la mesa.'
questions.a: Ponla.

days.guide: Your child records answers to 10 prompts, speaking for at least 30 seconds each, and self-scores with the rubric.

questions.q: Answer: '¿Qué hiciste el fin de semana?'
questions.a: Example: El sábado fui al cine con mi hermana y el domingo descansé en casa.

days.guide: Your child writes a 200-word narrative about a holiday meal, mixing imperfect (description) and preterite (events) with food vocabulary.

questions.q: Write: 'The table was full of food and we ate for three hours.'
questions.a: La mesa estaba llena de comida y comimos por tres horas.

days.guide: Your child rates the can-do statements, then takes the timed practice exam. Review errors and plan targeted review for next week.

questions.q: Fill in: Mientras mi tía ___ (cocinar), mis primos ___ (llegar).
questions.a: cocinaba; llegaron

weeks.assessment_key: Practice exam: score each section out of 25 (grammar, reading, writing, speaking). Sample items: 1) Me ___ (despertar) a las seis — despierto 2) De niño, ___ (ir) al parque — iba 3) Ayer ___ (hacer) la tarea — hice 4) Rewrite 'Corta la cebolla' with a pronoun — Córtala 5) Negative — No la cortes. Can-do self-assessment: student marks each statement 'I can do this easily / with help / not yet'; plan practice for 'not yet' items.

weeks.prep: Find or prepare two short audio clips (a restaurant order and a childhood memory — you can record a Spanish-speaking friend or use the UT Austin Spanish Proficiency Exercises) and a reading about a Latin American festival (e.g., Inti Raymi in Peru or Carnaval de Barranquilla). Prepare interview questions on routines, childhood, and food.
misconceptions: Panicking when not every word is understood: focus on main idea, key words, numbers, and cognates.
Giving one-word answers in the interview: expand with a detail and a reason (porque...).

days.guide: Play each clip twice. Your child answers comprehension questions; on the second listen, they confirm details.

questions.q: In a restaurant clip, a customer says 'Para mí, el pescado y un agua sin gas.' What did she order?
questions.a: The fish and a still (non-carbonated) water.

days.guide: Your child reads the festival article and answers main-idea and detail questions, underlining evidence.

questions.q: What is Inti Raymi?
questions.a: The Inca 'Festival of the Sun,' celebrated every June 24 in Cusco, Peru, around the winter solstice.

days.guide: Conduct the 5-minute interview: ¿Cómo es tu rutina? ¿Cómo eras de niño/a? ¿Qué comiste ayer? ¿Cuál es tu comida favorita? Score with the rubric.

questions.q: Answer with detail: '¿Cómo eras de niño/a?'
questions.a: Example: Era muy activo y un poco travieso. Siempre jugaba afuera con mis vecinos.

days.guide: Your child writes the 250-word email to a host family. Allow 40 minutes and no notes.

questions.q: Write a sentence about a recent celebration.
questions.a: Example: El mes pasado celebramos el cumpleaños de mi abuelo; comimos mole y bailamos toda la noche.

days.guide: Review results together. Your child writes three goals in Spanish for semester 2.

questions.q: Write a goal: 'I want to speak more in class.'
questions.a: Quiero hablar más en la clase.

weeks.assessment_key: Semester exam rubric across modes (4 levels each): Listening/Reading — 4 = main idea + most details correct; Speaking — 4 = 5 minutes sustained, accurate present/past tenses, asks a question back; Writing (250-word email) — 4 = greeting/closing, describes self (present), childhood (imperfect), recent celebration (preterite) with few errors; 3 = complete with some errors; 2 = missing a section or many errors; 1 = fragments. Sample reading answer for Inti Raymi: an Inca festival of the sun held June 24 in Cusco, Peru, at the winter solstice.

weeks.prep: Gather travel brochures or Spanish-language airline/hotel websites. Chart the future: infinitive + -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án; irregular stems tendr-, saldr-, pondr-, vendr-, podr-, sabr-, querr-, har-, dir-, habr-.
misconceptions: Adding endings to the stem instead of the infinitive (*hablé for future): the future attaches to the whole infinitive — hablaré.
Forgetting accents (*hablare): all forms except nosotros carry an accent — hablaré, hablarás, hablará, hablaremos, hablarán.
Regularizing irregulars (*teneré, *haceré): tendré, haré.

days.guide: Label pictures: el aeropuerto, el pasaporte, la maleta, el boleto, la tarjeta de embarque, el vuelo, la puerta, el hotel, la habitación, la recepción. Your child completes the matching drill.

questions.q: Give the Spanish for passport, suitcase, ticket, flight.
questions.a: el pasaporte, la maleta, el boleto (el billete in Spain), el vuelo

days.guide: Review ir a + infinitive (Voy a viajar). Your child writes 10 sentences about next weekend's plans.

questions.q: Translate: 'We are going to visit my cousins.'
questions.a: Vamos a visitar a mis primos (personal a before people).

days.guide: Teach the simple future endings and irregular stems; your child completes the drill and writes 5 predictions.

questions.q: Translate: 'I will have a lot of time and I will travel to Peru.'
questions.a: Tendré mucho tiempo y viajaré a Perú.

questions.q: Conjugate salir in the future for nosotros.
questions.a: saldremos

days.guide: Your child interviews a family member: ¿Adónde viajarás? ¿Con quién irás? ¿Qué harás allí? ¿Cuánto tiempo estarás? Notes go in third person (Mi papá viajará a...).

questions.q: Ask: 'What will you do there?'
questions.a: ¿Qué harás allí?

days.guide: Give the future-tense quiz.

questions.q: Fill in: Mañana ellos ___ (venir) y nosotros ___ (hacer) una fiesta.
questions.a: vendrán; haremos

weeks.assessment_key: Future quiz sample key: viajar/yo — viajaré; comer/tú — comerás; vivir/ellos — vivirán; tener/yo — tendré; salir/nosotros — saldremos; hacer/ella — hará; decir/ustedes — dirán; poder/tú — podrás; poner/yo — pondré; 'I am going to buy a ticket' — Voy a comprar un boleto.

weeks.prep: Print blank maps of Latin America, the Caribbean, and Spain. List the 21 Spanish-speaking countries and capitals (include Equatorial Guinea in Africa; Puerto Rico is a U.S. territory, often counted among the 21). Find an article on Machu Picchu or the Galápagos and weather reports for three capitals.
misconceptions: Thinking Brazil speaks Spanish: Brazil's language is Portuguese.
Bolivia's capital: Sucre is the constitutional capital and La Paz is the seat of government — both are acceptable if explained.
Using 'hace' with all weather: 'hace calor/frío/sol/viento' but 'está nublado,' 'llueve,' 'nieva.'

days.guide: Your child labels the countries and capitals, then quizzes with flashcards. Practice saying them with correct accents (Bogotá, Perú, Panamá).

questions.q: What is the capital of Peru and of Argentina?
questions.a: Lima; Buenos Aires

questions.q: Which Spanish-speaking country is in Africa?
questions.a: Equatorial Guinea (Guinea Ecuatorial), capital Malabo.

days.guide: Teach landform vocabulary (la montaña, la cordillera, la selva, el desierto, la costa, la isla, el río, el lago, el volcán). Your child writes sentences like 'Los Andes son la cordillera más larga del mundo.'

questions.q: Where is the Atacama Desert and what is notable about it?
questions.a: Northern Chile; it is one of the driest (non-polar) deserts in the world.

questions.q: Translate: 'Costa Rica has many volcanoes and beaches.'
questions.a: Costa Rica tiene muchos volcanes y playas.

days.guide: Your child reads the article and answers questions. For Machu Picchu: an Inca citadel built in the 1400s high in the Andes of Peru; for Galápagos: Ecuadorian islands whose unique wildlife influenced Darwin.

questions.q: Who built Machu Picchu and in which country is it?
questions.a: The Inca, in Peru (near Cusco).

questions.q: To which country do the Galápagos Islands belong?
questions.a: Ecuador.

days.guide: Your child compares the weather in three capitals: 'En Quito hace fresco; en La Habana hace calor y está nublado.' Mention that seasons are reversed south of the equator.

questions.q: If it is July, what season is it in Buenos Aires?
questions.a: Winter (el invierno) — the Southern Hemisphere's seasons are reversed.

questions.q: Translate: 'It's raining in Bogotá.'
questions.a: Llueve (Está lloviendo) en Bogotá.

days.guide: Give the map and geography quiz.

questions.q: What is the capital of Uruguay?
questions.a: Montevideo

weeks.assessment_key: Map quiz key (country — capital): México — Ciudad de México; Guatemala — Ciudad de Guatemala; El Salvador — San Salvador; Honduras — Tegucigalpa; Nicaragua — Managua; Costa Rica — San José; Panamá — Ciudad de Panamá; Cuba — La Habana; República Dominicana — Santo Domingo; Puerto Rico — San Juan; Colombia — Bogotá; Venezuela — Caracas; Ecuador — Quito; Perú — Lima; Bolivia — La Paz/Sucre; Chile — Santiago; Argentina — Buenos Aires; Uruguay — Montevideo; Paraguay — Asunción; España — Madrid; Guinea Ecuatorial — Malabo. Geography items: los Andes = mountains along western South America; el desierto de Atacama = Chile, one of the driest places on Earth; la selva amazónica = rainforest mainly in Brazil, Peru, Colombia.

weeks.prep: Print a tourist map of central Madrid (Puerta del Sol, Plaza Mayor, Museo del Prado, Parque del Retiro) or Mexico City's Centro Histórico. Prepare a por/para chart. Find a short Spanish tourism video (e.g., Turismo de España or Visit Mexico).
misconceptions: Using 'para' for 'through' or 'for (in exchange)': por = through/along, duration, exchange, means, cause; para = destination, purpose, deadline, recipient, opinion.
Confusing 'doblar' with 'double': in directions it means 'turn' (Dobla a la derecha).
Mixing tú and usted when asking strangers: use usted (Disculpe, ¿me puede decir...?).

days.guide: Teach siga derecho/sigue derecho, dobla/doble a la derecha/izquierda, cruza la calle, a dos cuadras, en la esquina, está al lado de/enfrente de. Your child traces routes on the Madrid map as you give directions.

questions.q: Translate: 'Go straight two blocks and turn left.'
questions.a: Sigue derecho dos cuadras y dobla a la izquierda. (Usted: Siga derecho... y doble...)

questions.q: What does 'la esquina' mean?
questions.a: The (street) corner.

days.guide: Teach a few anchors: por = 'through, by, for (exchange/duration), because of'; para = 'for (purpose), to (destination), by (deadline), for (recipient).' Your child completes 20 sentences with reasons.

questions.q: Choose por or para: 'Gracias ___ la ayuda.'
questions.a: por (cause/exchange)

questions.q: Choose: 'Salimos ___ México el viernes.'
questions.a: para (destination)

days.guide: You are a passerby in Madrid; your child is the tourist: 'Disculpe, ¿cómo llego al Museo del Prado?' Give 3-step directions; your child repeats them back.

questions.q: Ask politely in usted form: 'Excuse me, where is the station?'
questions.a: Disculpe, ¿dónde está la estación?

days.guide: Your child watches the tourism video and lists five recommended sites with one Spanish descriptive sentence each.

questions.q: Name two famous sites in Madrid.
questions.a: Examples: el Museo del Prado, el Parque del Retiro, la Plaza Mayor, el Palacio Real, la Puerta del Sol.

days.guide: Give the por/para quiz and score the role-play.

questions.q: Choose: 'Necesito el informe ___ mañana.'
questions.a: para (deadline)

weeks.assessment_key: Por/para quiz sample key: 1) Salgo ___ Madrid mañana — para (destination) 2) Caminamos ___ el parque — por (through) 3) Pagué 20 euros ___ la entrada — por (exchange) 4) Estudio ___ ser guía — para (purpose) 5) La tarea es ___ el lunes — para (deadline) 6) Viajamos ___ avión — en (or por) avión; accept 'en' as most common 7) Estuve en Sevilla ___ tres días — por (duration) 8) Este regalo es ___ ti — para (recipient). Role-play rubric: 4 = polite opening with usted, asks for directions, understands and repeats 3+ steps; 3 = minor errors; 2 = needs help; 1 = cannot complete.

weeks.prep: Help your child pick a Spanish-speaking city and bookmark Spanish-language tourism, museum, and hotel sites. Prepare a slide template and look up the local currency (euro, peso mexicano, sol peruano, peso colombiano, etc.) with a current exchange rate. Write the Unit 5 test (travel vocabulary, future, geography, directions, por/para).
misconceptions: Mixing currencies or forgetting conversion: state the exchange rate on the budget slide and convert all prices consistently.
Writing the itinerary in the present: plans should use the future (Visitaremos...) or ir a + infinitive.

days.guide: Your child researches sites, typical foods, and lodging on Spanish-language pages, taking notes in Spanish with prices.

questions.q: What is the currency of Spain and Mexico?
questions.a: Spain: el euro; Mexico: el peso mexicano.

days.guide: Your child writes a 5-day itinerary in the future tense with a budget table (lodging, food, transport, entry fees).

questions.q: Write: 'On the first day we will visit the cathedral.'
questions.a: El primer día visitaremos la catedral.

questions.q: If a hotel costs 80 euros per night for 4 nights, what is the total?
questions.a: 320 euros (convert to dollars with the current rate).

days.guide: Your child creates 8 slides with images and Spanish captions; check captions for future forms and accents.

questions.q: Write a caption: 'We will eat paella in Valencia.'
questions.a: Comeremos paella en Valencia.

days.guide: Your child presents for 3 minutes. Ask: ¿Cuánto costará el hotel? ¿Qué harás el último día?

questions.q: Answer: '¿Cuánto dinero necesitarás en total?'
questions.a: Example: Necesitaré unos mil doscientos euros en total.

days.guide: Give the Unit 5 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'I will leave for Lima on Friday.'
questions.a: Saldré para Lima el viernes.

weeks.assessment_key: Itinerary presentation rubric: 4 = 3 minutes in Spanish, 5 days with sites/food/lodging, budget in local currency with U.S. conversion, accurate future tense, answers questions; 3 = minor errors or slight gaps; 2 = missing days/budget or frequent errors; 1 = incomplete. Unit test sample: 1) iremos/haremos/tendré 2) Dobla a la derecha 3) por/para items with reasons 4) capital of Colombia — Bogotá 5) el boleto de ida y vuelta = round-trip ticket.

weeks.prep: Print a body diagram. Chart doler (me duele + singular, me duelen + plural) and illness vocabulary: la gripe, el resfriado, la tos, la fiebre, la alergia, el dolor de cabeza/garganta/estómago.
misconceptions: Using a possessive with body parts (*Me duele mi cabeza): Spanish uses the article — Me duele la cabeza.
Forgetting plural agreement: Me duelen los pies (plural subject).
Confusing 'tener fiebre' with 'estar fiebre': tener fiebre, tener tos, but estar enfermo/a, estar resfriado/a.

days.guide: Your child labels 30 body parts, then plays Simón dice (Simón dice: tócate la nariz) with family, taking turns as Simón.

questions.q: Give the Spanish for: shoulder, knee, elbow, back.
questions.a: el hombro, la rodilla, el codo, la espalda

days.guide: Model: 'Me duele la cabeza. A mi hermano le duelen los oídos.' Your child writes 10 sentences with different people and body parts.

questions.q: Translate: 'Her throat hurts.'
questions.a: Le duele la garganta.

questions.q: Translate: 'My eyes hurt.'
questions.a: Me duelen los ojos.

days.guide: Your child writes symptom descriptions for 10 illnesses (Con la gripe, tengo fiebre, me duele el cuerpo y estoy cansado/a).

questions.q: Describe allergy symptoms in Spanish.
questions.a: Con una alergia, estornudo mucho, tengo los ojos rojos y me pica la nariz.

days.guide: You are el médico: '¿Qué le pasa? ¿Desde cuándo? ¿Tiene fiebre?' Your child is the patient and describes symptoms using usted with you.

questions.q: How does a doctor ask 'What's wrong?' formally?
questions.a: ¿Qué le pasa? / ¿Qué tiene?

days.guide: Give the vocabulary quiz and score the role-play.

questions.q: Correct: 'Me duele mis pies.'
questions.a: Me duelen los pies.

weeks.assessment_key: Health vocabulary quiz sample key: la cabeza = head; la garganta = throat; el estómago = stomach; la espalda = back; el brazo = arm; la rodilla = knee; toser = to cough; estornudar = to sneeze; tener fiebre = to have a fever; 'My feet hurt' = Me duelen los pies. Doctor role-play rubric: 4 = greets, describes 3+ symptoms with doler/tener/estar correctly, answers the doctor's questions; 3 = minor errors; 2 = limited; 1 = cannot complete.

weeks.prep: Find a CDC en español pamphlet (cdc.gov/spanish) on handwashing or flu. Chart usted/ustedes commands: from yo, drop -o, opposite vowel (tome, beba, descanse); irregulars dé, esté, vaya, sea, sepa. Reflexive commands attach the pronoun (Lávese, Siéntense).
misconceptions: Using tú forms with a patient (*Toma): formal commands are tome, beba, descanse.
Dropping the accent when attaching pronouns: Lávese, Tómelo (accent keeps the stress).
Forgetting spelling changes: buscar → busque, llegar → llegue, empezar → empiece.

days.guide: Show the formation from yo (tengo → tenga, hago → haga). Your child conjugates 20 verbs for usted and ustedes.

questions.q: Give usted commands for tomar, comer, and salir.
questions.a: tome, coma, salga

questions.q: Give the ustedes command of ir.
questions.a: vayan

days.guide: Your child reads the pamphlet and lists the commands it uses with English meanings.

questions.q: A pamphlet says 'Cúbrase la boca al toser.' What does it mean?
questions.a: Cover your mouth when you cough.

days.guide: Your child writes 10 poster tips with formal commands (Lávese las manos con jabón por 20 segundos. Beba mucha agua.).

questions.q: Write: 'Get a lot of rest.'
questions.a: Descanse mucho.

questions.q: Write: 'Don't touch your eyes.'
questions.a: No se toque los ojos.

days.guide: You are the pharmacist. Your child describes symptoms; you give instructions (Tome una pastilla cada ocho horas). Your child repeats them back to confirm.

questions.q: What does 'Tome dos pastillas cada seis horas con comida' mean?
questions.a: Take two pills every six hours with food.

days.guide: Give the formal commands quiz.

questions.q: Make negative: 'Tome café.'
questions.a: No tome café.

weeks.assessment_key: Formal commands quiz sample key: tomar — tome/tomen; beber — beba/beban; descansar — descanse/descansen; evitar — evite/eviten; ir — vaya/vayan; ser — sea/sean; dar — dé/den; hacer — haga/hagan; lavarse las manos — Lávese las manos; negative with pronoun — No se toque la cara.

weeks.prep: Chart haber (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han) + participle (-ado/-ido) and irregular participles: hecho, dicho, escrito, visto, puesto, vuelto, roto, abierto, muerto, cubierto, resuelto. Set up a simple habit tracker for the week.
misconceptions: Making the participle agree (*Ella ha comida): after haber the participle never changes — Ella ha comido.
Splitting haber and the participle (*He no comido): negatives and pronouns go before haber — No lo he comido.
Regularizing irregulars (*hacido, *escribido): hecho, escrito.

days.guide: Model: 'Hoy he comido fruta y he caminado una milla.' Your child forms participles for regular verbs and memorizes the irregular list.

questions.q: Give the participles of abrir, ver, and romper.
questions.a: abierto, visto, roto

questions.q: Translate: 'We have eaten.'
questions.a: Hemos comido.

days.guide: Your child writes about healthy habits from the tracker (Esta semana he dormido ocho horas cada noche; no he tomado refrescos).

questions.q: Translate: 'This week I have drunk a lot of water.'
questions.a: Esta semana he bebido (he tomado) mucha agua.

days.guide: Your child interviews a family member with ¿Has...? questions (¿Has corrido un maratón? ¿Has visitado México?) and records answers.

questions.q: Ask: 'Have you ever seen a volcano?'
questions.a: ¿Alguna vez has visto un volcán?

questions.q: Answer negatively: 'No, I have never seen one.'
questions.a: No, nunca he visto uno.

days.guide: Your child writes a 10-item bucket list using ya, todavía no, and nunca.

questions.q: Translate: 'I have already learned to swim, but I have not traveled to Spain yet.'
questions.a: Ya he aprendido a nadar, pero todavía no he viajado a España.

days.guide: Give the present perfect quiz.

questions.q: Correct: 'Ellos han escribido la carta.'
questions.a: Ellos han escrito la carta.

weeks.assessment_key: Present perfect quiz sample key: comer/yo — he comido; hablar/tú — has hablado; vivir/ella — ha vivido; hacer/nosotros — hemos hecho; decir/ellos — han dicho; escribir/yo — he escrito; ver/tú — has visto; volver/ella — ha vuelto; poner/ustedes — han puesto; 'I have not done it yet' — Todavía no lo he hecho.

weeks.prep: Find short readings on remedios caseros (té de manzanilla for stomachaches, té de jengibre, miel con limón for sore throats, sábila/aloe for burns) and a simple comparison of health systems in Cuba (universal, state-run), Mexico (public IMSS/ISSSTE plus private), and the U.S. (mix of private insurance and public Medicare/Medicaid). Write the Unit 6 test (body, doler, formal commands, present perfect).
misconceptions: Presenting home remedies as medical cures: note they are cultural practices; serious symptoms need a doctor.
Overgeneralizing about whole countries: say 'muchas personas' rather than 'todos'.

days.guide: Read about remedios caseros; your child lists four and compares them to remedies their family uses.

questions.q: What is té de manzanilla traditionally used for?
questions.a: Chamomile tea is traditionally used to calm an upset stomach and help with relaxation/sleep.

days.guide: Read the short comparison; your child fills a three-column chart and writes 3 comparison sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'In Cuba, health care is free and public.'
questions.a: En Cuba, la atención médica es gratuita y pública.

days.guide: Your child scripts a 1-minute PSA (e.g., wash hands, sleep, hydration) using formal ustedes commands.

questions.q: Write an ustedes command: 'Wash your hands often.'
questions.a: Lávense las manos a menudo.

days.guide: Your child presents the PSA and explains the message in Spanish when you ask '¿Por qué es importante?'

questions.q: Answer: '¿Por qué es importante dormir bien?'
questions.a: Example: Es importante porque el cuerpo descansa y el cerebro funciona mejor.

days.guide: Give the Unit 6 test.

questions.q: Fill in: El médico ___ (decir) que yo ___ (tener) gripe. (present perfect + present)
questions.a: ha dicho; tengo

weeks.assessment_key: PSA rubric: 4 = 1 minute, clear health message, 4+ formal commands and accurate vocabulary, engaging visuals/delivery; 3 = minor errors; 2 = unclear message or many errors; 1 = incomplete. Unit test sample: 1) Me duelen las piernas 2) usted commands: beba, descanse, vaya 3) he hecho, ha dicho, hemos visto 4) la tos = cough; estornudar = to sneeze.

weeks.prep: Print a simple map of your town. Find an article on teen volunteers in Latin America — TECHO (founded in Chile in 1997) builds emergency housing with young volunteers. Prepare community vocabulary: el ayuntamiento/la alcaldía, la estación de bomberos, la comisaría, la biblioteca, el hospital, el comedor de beneficencia.
misconceptions: Confusing 'el bombero' (firefighter) with 'la bomba' (bomb/pump).
Mixing preterite and present perfect: preterite for a finished time (El verano pasado ayudé...), present perfect for life experience (He ayudado...).

days.guide: Your child draws a town map with 15 places and labels the job done at each (En la estación de bomberos trabajan los bomberos).

questions.q: Translate: 'The library is next to the park.'
questions.a: La biblioteca está al lado del parque.

questions.q: Who works at a hospital?
questions.a: los médicos y los enfermeros (las enfermeras)

days.guide: Read about TECHO or a similar group; your child answers main-idea and detail questions.

questions.q: What does TECHO do?
questions.a: It mobilizes young volunteers to build emergency housing and work with families in poor communities across Latin America; it started in Chile.

days.guide: Your child interviews someone: ¿Has trabajado como voluntario? ¿Dónde ayudaste? ¿Qué hiciste? Notes use present perfect and preterite.

questions.q: Ask: 'Have you ever volunteered?'
questions.a: ¿Alguna vez has trabajado como voluntario/a?

days.guide: Your child writes a 150-word paragraph about a real or possible volunteer project explaining who it helps.

questions.q: Translate: 'I could help at a soup kitchen.'
questions.a: Podría ayudar en un comedor de beneficencia.

days.guide: Give the vocabulary quiz and the 2-minute oral map description.

questions.q: Translate: 'The fire station is across from the school.'
questions.a: La estación de bomberos está enfrente de la escuela.

weeks.assessment_key: Vocabulary quiz sample key: el bombero = firefighter; el ayuntamiento = city hall; el comedor de beneficencia = soup kitchen; el/la voluntario/a = volunteer; ayudar = to help; la biblioteca = library; el cartero = mail carrier; el/la enfermero/a = nurse. Oral map description rubric: 4 = 2 minutes, 10+ places with location phrases (al lado de, cerca de) and jobs; 3 = 7–9 places; 2 = under 7; 1 = list only.

weeks.prep: Gather Spanish articles on Amazon deforestation and Mexico City air quality (BBC Mundo, El País) and set out household bins. Prepare a short Spanish news clip on drought or air quality. Choose an unseen environmental article for Friday.
misconceptions: Using 'reciclar' as a noun: el reciclaje is the noun; reciclar is the verb.
Assuming Mexico City's smog comes only from cars: its high altitude basin surrounded by mountains traps pollution, combined with vehicles and industry.

days.guide: Teach 25 terms with images (la contaminación, la deforestación, la sequía, reciclar, proteger, los recursos naturales, la basura, el calentamiento global). Your child writes one sentence about California for each.

questions.q: Translate: 'California has a lot of drought.'
questions.a: En California hay mucha sequía.

questions.q: What does 'proteger los recursos naturales' mean?
questions.a: To protect natural resources.

days.guide: Your child reads the Amazon article and fills a cause/effect chart.

questions.q: Name two causes of Amazon deforestation.
questions.a: Cattle ranching (la ganadería), agriculture such as soy, logging, mining, and fires/clearing for farmland.

questions.q: Name one effect.
questions.a: Loss of biodiversity and habitat; more carbon dioxide in the atmosphere; harm to Indigenous communities.

days.guide: Your child sorts one day's trash and recycling, counts items, and writes a short report in Spanish.

questions.q: Translate: 'We threw away eight plastic bottles.'
questions.a: Tiramos ocho botellas de plástico.

days.guide: Watch the news clip; your child compares Mexico City and Los Angeles (both basins surrounded by mountains, with car-related smog and water stress).

questions.q: Why do Mexico City and Los Angeles both have smog problems?
questions.a: Both sit in basins surrounded by mountains that trap polluted air, and both have heavy vehicle traffic.

days.guide: Your child reads an unseen article and answers comprehension questions.

questions.q: What is 'la sequía'?
questions.a: Drought.

weeks.assessment_key: Recycling report rubric: 4 = quantities for each category (Tiramos 12 botellas de plástico...), a conclusion, and 2 recommendations in Spanish; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = incomplete data; 1 = mostly English. Reading check: answers must cite the unseen article's main idea, one cause, one effect, and one solution.

weeks.prep: Make a subjunctive chart: yo present → drop -o → opposite endings (-ar: -e, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en; -er/-ir: -a, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an). Irregulars: dar (dé), ir (vaya), ser (sea), estar (esté), saber (sepa), haber (haya).
misconceptions: Using the subjunctive without a change of subject: 'Quiero ir' (same subject, infinitive) vs. 'Quiero que tú vayas' (different subjects, subjunctive).
Forgetting 'que' after the trigger: Es importante que reciclemos.
Using the subjunctive after ojalá in a different way: ojalá is always followed by the subjunctive (Ojalá que llueva).

days.guide: Teach the 'opposite vowel' rule from the yo form (tengo → tenga, hago → haga, digo → diga). Your child conjugates 20 verbs.

questions.q: Give the subjunctive yo form of tener, salir, and conocer.
questions.a: tenga, salga, conozca

questions.q: Give the subjunctive of ir for nosotros.
questions.a: vayamos

days.guide: Model: 'Recomiendo que tomemos duchas cortas.' Your child writes 10 water-saving recommendations to family members.

questions.q: Translate: 'I suggest that my brother turn off the water.'
questions.a: Sugiero que mi hermano cierre el agua (or apague la llave).

questions.q: Translate: 'I recommend that we use less water.'
questions.a: Recomiendo que usemos menos agua.

days.guide: Your child completes 15 sentences with es importante/necesario/mejor que + subjunctive.

questions.q: Complete: 'Es necesario que nosotros ___ (proteger) el planeta.'
questions.a: protejamos (g → j spelling change)

days.guide: Your child writes five wishes with ojalá and reads them aloud.

questions.q: Translate: 'I hope there are more parks.'
questions.a: Ojalá (que) haya más parques.

days.guide: Give the subjunctive quiz.

questions.q: Correct: 'Es importante que nosotros reciclamos.'
questions.a: Es importante que nosotros reciclemos.

weeks.assessment_key: Subjunctive quiz sample key: hablar/yo — hable; comer/tú — comas; vivir/nosotros — vivamos; tener/ella — tenga; hacer/ellos — hagan; ir/yo — vaya; ser/tú — seas; dar/él — dé; 'It's important that we recycle' — Es importante que reciclemos; 'I recommend that you (tú) save water' — Te recomiendo que ahorres agua.

weeks.prep: Gather poster board or a video app. Help your child pick a local problem (plastic on beaches, water waste, litter in parks). Write the Unit 7 test (community, environment, subjunctive with recommendations and ojalá).
misconceptions: Writing slogans as literal translations: keep them short and catchy in Spanish (¡Cuida el agua, cuida la vida!).
Mixing tú and usted commands on one poster: choose one register for the campaign.

days.guide: Your child chooses a problem and lists 5–8 facts in Spanish from reliable sources.

questions.q: Write a fact: 'Every year, millions of tons of plastic end up in the ocean.'
questions.a: Cada año, millones de toneladas de plástico terminan en el océano.

days.guide: Your child writes 3 slogans and 8 recommendations (Recoja su basura. Es necesario que usemos botellas reutilizables.).

questions.q: Write a usted command: 'Use reusable bags.'
questions.a: Use bolsas reutilizables.

questions.q: Write a subjunctive recommendation: 'It's better that people walk.'
questions.a: Es mejor que la gente camine.

days.guide: Your child designs the bilingual poster or 60-second video; check Spanish accuracy before finalizing.

questions.q: Create a slogan about water.
questions.a: Example: ¡Cada gota cuenta! / ¡Cuida el agua, cuida la vida!

days.guide: Your child presents the campaign and answers two questions in Spanish (¿Qué puede hacer una familia? ¿Por qué es importante?).

questions.q: Answer: '¿Qué puede hacer una familia?'
questions.a: Example: Una familia puede reciclar, usar menos plástico y tomar duchas más cortas.

days.guide: Give the Unit 7 test.

questions.q: Fill in: Ojalá que mi comunidad ___ (tener) más árboles.
questions.a: tenga

weeks.assessment_key: Campaign rubric: 4 = accurate facts, 3 slogans, 8 recommendations using formal commands and subjunctive correctly, clear visuals, answers 2 questions; 3 = minor errors; 2 = fewer recommendations or many errors; 1 = incomplete. Unit test sample: 1) Es importante que (nosotros) apaguemos las luces 2) Ojalá que no haya contaminación 3) la sequía = drought 4) Recicle las botellas (usted command).

weeks.prep: Bookmark images of Frida Kahlo's 'Las dos Fridas' (1939, Museo de Arte Moderno, Mexico City) and Diego Rivera's 'Detroit Industry' murals (1932–33, Detroit Institute of Arts) or 'Pan American Unity' (1940, San Francisco). Preview: Kahlo's art shows injury and pain; some images include blood or exposed hearts.
misconceptions: Thinking Kahlo painted mostly landscapes: about a third of her works are self-portraits (autorretratos).
Using 'pintura' only for paint: la pintura = painting (art form) or paint; el cuadro = a painting (artwork).

days.guide: Teach 20 terms; your child describes one painting (A la izquierda hay..., en el fondo se ve..., los colores son...).

questions.q: Translate: 'In the background there are clouds.'
questions.a: En el fondo hay nubes.

days.guide: Read a short Kahlo biography (bus accident at 18, years of pain and surgeries, marriage to Diego Rivera, Mexican identity). Your child explains how her life appears in 'Las dos Fridas.'

questions.q: What does 'Las dos Fridas' show?
questions.a: Two Fridas seated hand in hand — one in a European-style white dress, one in a Tehuana (Mexican) dress — with their hearts exposed and connected by an artery; it reflects her dual heritage and her pain after her divorce from Rivera.

questions.q: Why did Kahlo paint so many self-portraits?
questions.a: She spent long periods alone and bedridden after her accident; she said she painted herself because she was the subject she knew best.
