days.guide: Look at the Detroit Industry murals; your child describes the workers, machines, and colors.

questions.q: What do the Detroit Industry murals show?
questions.a: Workers at the Ford River Rouge auto plant building cars, with huge machines — celebrating industry and labor.

days.guide: Your child writes opinions on two works using me parece que, creo que, me gusta porque.

questions.q: Write an opinion sentence about a mural.
questions.a: Example: Me parece que el mural es impresionante porque muestra a muchos trabajadores juntos.

days.guide: Give the vocabulary quiz and the 1-minute oral description.

questions.q: Translate: 'self-portrait'
questions.a: el autorretrato

weeks.assessment_key: Art vocabulary quiz sample key: el cuadro = painting; el mural = mural; el autorretrato = self-portrait; el fondo = background; en primer plano = in the foreground; el pintor/la pintora = painter; los colores vivos = bright colors; me parece que = it seems to me that. Oral description rubric: 4 = 1 minute, describes colors, figures, placement (a la izquierda, en el fondo), and gives an opinion with reason; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = list of words; 1 = minimal.

weeks.prep: Bookmark the Museo del Prado online collection: 'Las Meninas' (Velázquez, 1656), Goya's 'El 3 de mayo de 1808' and 'El quitasol'. Find Picasso's 'Las Meninas' series (1957, Museu Picasso, Barcelona). Chart comparatives and irregular forms.
misconceptions: Saying 'más bueno' or 'más malo' for quality: use mejor/peor.
Using 'que' with tan (*tan alto que): equality uses tan + adjective + como.
Using 'en' in superlatives (*el más alto en la familia): Spanish uses de — el más alto de la familia.

days.guide: Teach más/menos + adjective + que and tan + adjective + como; your child writes 10 sentences comparing family members.

questions.q: Translate: 'My sister is as tall as my mother.'
questions.a: Mi hermana es tan alta como mi mamá.

questions.q: Translate: 'I am less patient than my father.'
questions.a: Soy menos paciente que mi papá.

days.guide: Teach el/la/los/las + más + adjective + de and irregular mejor, peor, mayor, menor.

questions.q: Translate: 'She is the best student in the class.'
questions.a: Es la mejor estudiante de la clase.

questions.q: Translate: 'This is the worst movie of the year.'
questions.a: Es la peor película del año.

days.guide: Take the Prado online tour; your child chooses one Velázquez and one Goya work and notes title, date, and description.

questions.q: Who painted 'Las Meninas' and whom does it show?
questions.a: Diego Velázquez (1656); it shows the young Infanta Margarita with her maids of honor (las meninas), Velázquez himself painting, and the king and queen reflected in a mirror.

days.guide: Your child compares Velázquez's 'Las Meninas' with one of Picasso's 1957 versions using at least six comparatives.

questions.q: Write: 'Picasso's version is more abstract than Velázquez's.'
questions.a: La versión de Picasso es más abstracta que la de Velázquez.

days.guide: Give the comparatives quiz, then rank three paintings in conversation (Para mí, el mejor es... porque...).

questions.q: Translate: 'It is the most famous painting in the museum.'
questions.a: Es el cuadro más famoso del museo.

weeks.assessment_key: Comparatives quiz sample key: 1) Mi hermano es más alto que yo 2) La pintura es tan bonita como el mural 3) Tengo tantos libros como tú 4) Este cuadro es el más famoso del museo 5) Goya es mejor que... (opinion; check structure) 6) mi hermana mayor = my older sister. Conversation rubric: 4 = ranks three paintings with 5+ correct comparatives/superlatives and reasons; 3 = minor errors; 2 = few comparisons; 1 = minimal.

weeks.prep: Make a playlist: salsa (e.g., Celia Cruz), cumbia (Colombian cumbia), flamenco (Paco de Lucía), mariachi (Vicente Fernández or Mariachi Vargas), son jarocho ('La Bamba'). Print lyrics for 'La Bamba' (traditional son jarocho from Veracruz). Preview 'Latinoamérica' by Calle 13 if used (clean, but politically themed).
misconceptions: Thinking 'La Bamba' is originally a rock song: it is a traditional son jarocho from Veracruz, Mexico, made famous in rock form by Ritchie Valens in 1958.
Placing flamenco in Latin America: flamenco comes from Andalusia in southern Spain, with Romani (gitano), Moorish, and Andalusian roots.

days.guide: Play a clip of each genre; your child notes instruments and rhythm in Spanish (la guitarra, la trompeta, el violín, los tambores, las palmas).

questions.q: Where is mariachi music from and what instruments does it use?
questions.a: Jalisco, Mexico — violins, trumpets, guitar, vihuela, and guitarrón (bass).

days.guide: Read the 'La Bamba' lyrics; your child identifies the theme (dancing la bamba requires 'una poca de gracia') and playful lines like 'Yo no soy marinero, soy capitán.'

questions.q: What does 'Para bailar la bamba se necesita una poca de gracia' mean?
questions.a: To dance la bamba you need a little grace.

days.guide: Your child researches one genre's African, Indigenous, and European roots and writes a paragraph.

questions.q: What are the roots of cumbia?
questions.a: It began on Colombia's Caribbean coast, blending African drums and rhythms, Indigenous flutes (gaitas), and European/Spanish melodies and later instruments.

days.guide: Your child builds a 6-song playlist with a Spanish description of each (genre, country, opinion).

questions.q: Write a description: 'This salsa song is very energetic and makes me want to dance.'
questions.a: Esta canción de salsa es muy enérgica y me dan ganas de bailar.

days.guide: Give the listening quiz (identify genres) and lyric comprehension questions.

questions.q: Where does flamenco come from?
questions.a: Andalusia, in southern Spain.

weeks.assessment_key: Listening quiz key: identify each clip — salsa (Afro-Cuban rhythms, clave, brass, developed in New York); cumbia (Colombian Caribbean coast, African drums, Indigenous gaitas/flutes, European elements); flamenco (Andalusia, Spain: guitar, cante, palmas); mariachi (Jalisco, Mexico: violins, trumpets, vihuela, guitarrón); son jarocho (Veracruz, Mexico: jarana, requinto, harp, zapateado). Lyric comprehension: answers must match the provided lyrics. Annotated playlist rubric: 4 = 6 songs, genre/country, 2–3 accurate Spanish sentences each with opinion; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = fewer songs or English; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Prepare a slide template and museum websites (Prado, MoMA, Museo Frida Kahlo, Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes). Write the Unit 8 test (art vocabulary, comparatives/superlatives, music genres).
misconceptions: Copying labels from websites: labels must be the child's own Spanish, citing facts.
Listing works without a theme: the exhibit needs a unifying theme (family, identity, nature) explained in the introduction panel.

days.guide: Your child selects five works or songs from at least three countries around a theme and writes why each fits.

questions.q: Give a possible theme title in Spanish.
questions.a: Example: La identidad en el arte hispano / La naturaleza en el arte

days.guide: Your child writes an 80-word label for each work: artist, date, description, opinion.

questions.q: Write a label opening for 'Las dos Fridas.'
questions.a: Las dos Fridas (1939), Frida Kahlo, México. Óleo sobre lienzo. La obra muestra dos versiones de la artista...

days.guide: Your child builds the slides with an introduction panel explaining the theme.

questions.q: Write an introduction sentence.
questions.a: Example: Bienvenidos a nuestra exposición sobre la identidad. Aquí van a ver obras de México, España y Cuba.

days.guide: Your child gives a 4-minute tour in Spanish, using at least five comparatives/superlatives.

questions.q: Write a tour sentence with a superlative.
questions.a: Example: Este es el cuadro más colorido de la exposición.

days.guide: Give the Unit 8 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'The mural is bigger than the painting.'
questions.a: El mural es más grande que el cuadro.

weeks.assessment_key: Exhibit rubric: 4 = 5 works from 3+ countries, clear theme, 80-word labels with artist/date/description/opinion, 4-minute tour with comparatives; 3 = minor gaps; 2 = fewer works or weak Spanish; 1 = incomplete. Unit test sample: 1) el autorretrato = self-portrait 2) tan + adj + como 3) mejor/peor 4) flamenco — España 5) Frida Kahlo — México.

weeks.prep: Print a script template with four sections (childhood, memorable event, routine, future) and a checklist of tenses and agreement. Have a phone/camera and simple video editor ready. Schedule a 20-minute script conference on day 3.
misconceptions: Mixing tenses across sections: imperfect for childhood description, preterite for the event, present for routine, future for plans.
Writing too complex sentences from English: keep to structures you know and use connectors (además, sin embargo, por eso).

days.guide: Your child outlines the 4-minute video with key sentences and visuals for each section.

questions.q: Write one sentence for each tense about yourself.
questions.a: Example: De niño vivía en Fresno (imperfect). En 2020 fui a México (preterite). Ahora me levanto a las siete (present). En el futuro estudiaré medicina (future).

days.guide: Your child writes a 500+ word script and self-edits with the checklist, underlining each verb and labeling its tense.

questions.q: Fix: 'El año pasado iba a Guatemala por una semana.'
questions.a: El año pasado fui a Guatemala por una semana (completed trip = preterite).

days.guide: Hold a conference: read the script aloud together, focusing on accuracy and adding connectors. Your child revises.

questions.q: Use 'sin embargo' in a sentence.
questions.a: Example: Me gusta mi ciudad; sin embargo, quiero vivir en otro país algún día.

days.guide: Your child records the video with visuals and Spanish subtitles, re-recording any section with errors.

questions.q: Translate: 'In ten years, I will live in a big city.'
questions.a: En diez años viviré en una ciudad grande.

days.guide: Hold a family premiere; family members ask questions in Spanish, and your child answers.

questions.q: Answer: '¿Qué harás después de graduarte?'
questions.a: Example: Después de graduarme, iré a la universidad y estudiaré biología.

weeks.assessment_key: Final video rubric (4 levels per row): Content — all four sections, ~4 minutes; Language — accurate imperfect, preterite, present, and future with 4+ connectors; Delivery — clear pronunciation, not reading; Production — visuals and Spanish subtitles. 4 = excellent on all rows; 3 = minor issues; 2 = missing a section or many errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Prepare a mixed grammar drill and a vocabulary game (e.g., Pictionary or Quizlet Live) covering all units. Find a short travel podcast clip (e.g., from a Spanish learner podcast) and a short newspaper article. Plan the 6-minute interview with a pharmacy or hotel role-play.
misconceptions: Using the indicative after recommendations (*Te recomiendo que estudias): use the subjunctive — estudies.
Forgetting usted forms in the role-play: speak to the pharmacist or receptionist with usted.

days.guide: Your child completes the mixed grammar drill and plays the vocabulary game. Review any weak area.

questions.q: Give: preterite yo of ir, imperfect yo of ver, future yo of tener, subjunctive yo of hacer.
questions.a: fui, veía, tendré, haga

days.guide: Play the podcast clip twice and give the article; your child answers comprehension questions.

questions.q: What strategy helps with a fast podcast?
questions.a: Listen first for the main idea, then listen again for key details, numbers, and names; use cognates and context.

days.guide: Hold the 6-minute interview with a hotel or pharmacy role-play (Quisiera una habitación doble por tres noches / ¿Tiene algo para la tos?).

questions.q: Ask a hotel clerk for a double room for two nights.
questions.a: Quisiera una habitación doble por dos noches, por favor.

days.guide: Your child writes the 300-word letter to a future Spanish III student with commands and subjunctive advice.

questions.q: Write two pieces of advice.
questions.a: Example: Estudia el vocabulario cada día. Te recomiendo que hables con hispanohablantes.

days.guide: Your child completes the can-do self-assessment and writes Spanish III goals in Spanish.

questions.q: Write a goal: 'Next year I want to read a novel in Spanish.'
questions.a: El próximo año quiero leer una novela en español.

weeks.assessment_key: Final exam rubric (4 levels per mode): Interpretive — main idea and most details; Interpersonal — 6 minutes, handles the role-play, asks and answers questions with mostly accurate tenses; Presentational (300-word letter) — advice with 4+ tú commands and 4+ subjunctive recommendations (Te recomiendo que estudies...; Es importante que practiques...), clear organization. Sample correct forms: Practica todos los días; No tengas miedo; Es importante que hables mucho; Te recomiendo que uses Conjuguemos.
